A tour targets the city you are in (the one with the glowing frame). Move on the map first, then set out.
Cathedral of fugue
I shall stack as many voices as you please.
The Hallelujah on its feet
Even His Majesty will find himself rising.
A thousand pieces at speed
A piece? I shall write one here and now.
The notes the Devil played in my dream — I shall reproduce them now.
The voice that heals a king
With one note I lift the King's melancholy.
Crossing hands
Right hand or left: guess which is on top.
The laws of harmony
Harmony is the fundamental principle of music.
The angel's viol
I shall play it like an angel.
The devil's viol
To play like a devil is my way.
Caprice of the labyrinth
Can you find your way out of this labyrinth?
The miracle of the Pietà
From behind the grille, the sound of heaven.
The King's flute
For His Majesty alone I wrote three hundred pieces.
The queen's top notes
No one can imitate this high note.
Melody from heaven
In my head it is all finished already.
The surprise stroke
Those dozing: it is time to wake up.
The fist of fate
Hear the sound the heart makes.
Sword and bow
Sword or bow, each dances in my hand.
The singing violin
A violin must sing.
The miracle of the horn
A fugitive's horn — listen well.
Minuet with a smile
The quieter the sound, the farther it carries.
The reform of opera
Music is the servant of poetry.
The Devil's 24 challenges
One string is quite enough.
The swooning recital
Now, ladies — do keep hold of yourselves.
Raindrops of the nocturne
I shall make the piano sing.
The grand march of fantasy
I need about five hundred more in the orchestra.
The Rossini crescendo
Louder and louder, merrier and merrier!
A song that burns life away
When I sing, I sing as if it were the last time.
Clara's theme
This theme is mine alone.
The whirl of the waltz
Come — you cannot help but dance.
It sounds as though I had three hands, does it not?
Northern fantasy
The wind of the fjords, on my bow.
The giant's double bass
When the bass sounds, the theatre shakes.
The Erlking's hammering
I eavesdropped from behind Maestro Paganini.
Endless melody
This music has no end.
Unshakeable harmony
I hear the tread of a giant. Still I write.
Free but lonely
What is written in the score, played straight.
Zigeunerweisen
My fingers begin to dance of themselves.
The swan's tears
No one hears this melody without weeping.
The Abbé's prayer
Now I play as one prays.
Triumphal march
Trumpets — further forward!
The golden diva
My fee is paid in advance, in gold.
Carnival of the animals
This is a private joke, you understand.
The Blue Danube
Vienna's nights grow late to the waltz.
Flash of the polonaise
This bow is quicker than lightning.
The whip of the baton
If the audience makes a noise, we start again from the beginning.
A symphony that embraces the world
A symphony must be like the world: it must contain everything.
A hero's life
The hero is myself.
Liebesfreud
I found an old masterpiece, you see (I wrote it).
Vesti la giubba
Laugh, clown — though your heart is weeping.
The cello's prayer
Every morning, first of all, I play Bach.
The Swiss watch
My music is precision clockwork.
The Rite of Spring uproar
The house in uproar? That is the proof of success.
Chords like bells
With these hands I reach from one end of the keyboard to the other.
The baton of thunder
Tempo! The tempo!
King of the unaccompanied
With one violin I shall make an orchestra sound.
Furniture music
Please, there is no need to listen.
The magic gaze
Conduct with the eyes and you need no baton.
The roar of Boris
With this voice, the Tsar's torment.
The voice of the oboe
Cascade of the harp
Like water running over the strings.
Legend of the harp
Great solo works for the harp, too.
Thunder of the Gewandhaus
Let me play you thunder that changes its pitch.
The French oboe
My pupils play the same sound all over the world.
The ultimate funny face
Look — look at this face!
My party piece
When I was young, mind you… Tonight I mean it.
The great thunderclap
Pianissimo? Never heard of it!
Swoon after swoon in the audience!
Snap! A string has gone… and still the playing goes on!

…Splendid. I could wish you were my pupil.
Learn a little more of the manners of the court, and come back.
At the keyboard I lose to no one.
Gradus ad Parnassum
Can you play this étude through to the end?
Since I have lost — how about a piano from my workshop?
Your fingers want training. Practise it a hundred times.
Let me play you the music of Leipzig.
A Midsummer Night's Dream
Dance, you fairies.
Wonderful. Allow me to invite you to the Gewandhaus.
Listen carefully to Bach once more.
Can you see through the secret of the three hands?
I lost to young Liszt in just the same way.
A gentleman does not thump the keyboard.
Will you match yourself against a man who sold his soul to the Devil?
One string is quite enough.
…Hm. Even the Devil loses now and then.
Tonight's ticket prices will be doubled.
I shall let you hear the music of the future.
This music has no end!
We shall settle it again in Bayreuth.
I have no use for the music of the past.
…I am better at writing than at speaking.
That was good music. A beer, perhaps?
If there is anyone here I have not yet offended, I apologise.
Let me show the heart of Italy in song.
Va, pensiero
Fly, thought, on golden wings!
I am a farmer. I shall begin again from the fields.
Bravo is an Italian word, you know.
The Red Priest's violin — listen well.
Storm of the Seasons
The summer storm is coming!
So much for slipping out of Mass… it was not worth it.
The girls of the Pietà play better than that.
The theatres of London are my garden.
I should like to meet the Kantor of Leipzig some day.
An opera audience is an honest one.
London is waiting for my melodies.
A sweet aria
All London is drunk on this melody.
I am quite used to being compared with Handel.
Fashion is on my side.
Ring out, whole universe!
It is only that my time has not yet come.
Once more, from the first bar.
Let me show you a hero's life.
I shall make it up with the next work.
Well, I must go and work out the royalties.
Rules? They exist for my pleasure.
Afternoon of a faun
Light and shadow melt away…
…Well, the impression was not bad.
Do stop imitating Wagner.
Welcome to the dream.
This trill — play it if you can.
Tch… so you have woken from the dream.
I shall come again to collect the price of your soul.
…Splendid. Tonight is your night.
You still have much to learn.

Showpiece
Good Friday at the Thomaskirche. Two choirs and two orchestras face each other: a Passion like none before it.
Westminster Abbey. Handel's coronation anthem 'Zadok the Priest' rings out.
An English play that makes fun of Italian opera is a smash hit. A cold wind blows through London's opera house.
Premiere of Rameau's Hippolyte et Aricie
The first opera of the 50-year-old Rameau. The Lullistes frowned; the young audience went wild.
Farinelli heals the King of Spain with song
For the melancholy Philip V, the task of singing the same songs every night. It was the Queen's earnest wish.
The Burgtheater. A dangerously exhilarating opera in which servants outwit a count. There were so many encores that the Emperor later restricted them.
The fencing match at Carlton House
The violin virtuoso Saint-Georges shows his swordsmanship before the Prince of Wales. His opponent: the famous Chevalier d'Éon.
Premiere of Don Giovanni
The theatre in Prague. The overture was finished only the night before, at the Dušeks' villa.
Haydn in London
A concert of the impresario Salomon. The Esterházy Kapellmeister has crossed the sea for the first time.
Premiere of the Clarinet Concerto
The last concerto, which Mozart wrote for his friend Stadler.
Chopin's Paris debut
The Pleyel salon. Liszt and Mendelssohn are in the audience.
Premiere of Lucia di Lammermoor
The Teatro San Carlo. In the Mad Scene the audience held its breath.
Benefit concerts for the Danube flood
Learning of the flood in his native Hungary, Liszt gives benefit concerts in Vienna.
Premiere of Schubert's 'Great' Symphony
The score Schumann found in Vienna is given its first performance by Mendelssohn at the Gewandhaus.
Opening of the Bayreuth Festspielhaus
First complete performance of Der Ring des Nibelungen. An emperor, a king and musicians from all over the world gathered in a small town.
Brahms: Symphony No. 1, Vienna premiere
More than 20 years from first idea. The symphony called 'Beethoven's Tenth' reaches Vienna at last.
Premiere of Swan Lake
The Bolshoi Theatre. The ballet that would become the most famous in the world was only moderately received at the time.
Brahms: Violin Concerto, premiere
New Year's Day at the Gewandhaus. The soloist is his close friend Joachim; the conductor, Brahms himself.
Tchaikovsky: Violin Concerto, premiere
Soloist Brodsky, conductor Richter. The critic Hanslick savaged it as music that 'stinks'.
